title: On‑Prem Upgrade Safety & API Compatibility Advisory (draft)
content:
Summary:
This advisory collects safety guidance, lightweight checklists, and Terraform module notes for performing upgrades of Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) control plane and runtime components. Focus is on minimizing customer downtime and ensuring API/ABI compatibility for in-place upgrades and reversible migrations. This is an operational draft — meant to be used by on-call/ops + solutions engineers during scheduled maintenance windows.

Goals and constraints:
- Maintain API contract (REST and internal gRPC) compatibility for supported client versions.
- Avoid irreversible data migrations where possible; if performed, provide robust rollback steps.
- Preserve customer KV/LLM cache integrity or provide safe invalidation patterns.
- Keep terraform state drift risk low; document provider upgrade impacts.
- Allow fast rollback path that restores serving within SLOs (<5m for simple restarts, <30m for DB rollback scenarios).

Pre-upgrade validation (run this in staging first):
1) Compatibility checklist:
   - Collect server-side API schema versions (openapi.yaml, internal gRPC proto SHAs).
   - Run compatibility tool: compare previous release API schema vs candidate. Flag breaking changes: removed endpoints, changed request/response required fields, or enum removals.
   - Verify SDK client codegen tests pass for major client languages (python/js/go).
2) Binary + model runtime tests:
   - Smoke start/stop on staging nodes with identical k8s node sizes.
   - Run KV cache warmup & replay tests; confirm cache keys serialize/deserialize between versions.
   - Hot-path latency bench: generate representative traffic and measure p50/p95.
3) Data migration dry run (if applicable):
   - Snapshot DB and run migration in isolated staging using the same migration flags.
   - Confirm forward and backward migration script exists (down migration).

Terraform / infra notes (brief, ops-facing):
- Provider pinning: do not bump cloud provider or terraform core in the same change as a runtime upgrade. Keep provider versions pinned in modules/providers.tf.
- Resource renames: to rename resources without destroying, use terraform state mv before applying. Document exact state mv commands in the PR description.
- Module interface changes: when a module signature changes (new required variable), provide a two-step rollout: first deploy module with new optional var with a default; second PR flip to required and remove default.
- State locking: ensure exclusive apply using remote state locking (s3/dynamodb or GCS). Schedule window and notify channels.
- Example commands (ops):
   - terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars -out=plan.tfout
   - terraform apply plan.tfout
   - terraform state mv module.old_resource.module resourcetype.new_name

Runtime upgrade strategy (control plane and agents):
1) Canary waves:
   - Wave 0: single control-plane replica + 1 agent in isolated AZ (smoke). Run full smoke tests.
   - Wave 1: 5% of agents (or single VPC) attached to new control-plane image, monitor for 30–60 minutes.
   - Wave 2: 25%, then 50%, then 100% — each step with automated rollback checkpoints.
2) Blue/Green for control plane where supported: bring up green control plane, update routing (internal LB) for a subset of customers, health-check loop before shifting more traffic.
3) Agent rollouts: prefer sequential rolling restarts with health probes (not full replace) to preserve local caches. If binary change incompatible with on-disk cache, schedule cache invalidation window.

API compatibility and consumer signaling:
- Tolerate unknown fields in responses (server-side must preserve unknown fields for forwards compatibility).
- If a request parameter is deprecated, keep support for it for at least two release cycles and emit deprecation header (X-Redwood-Deprecation).
- For breaking changes, require an explicit migration guide and a feature flag for a least one release.

Rollback playbook (fast paths and data fallbacks):
Fast rollback (control-plane binary):
- If new control-plane is unhealthy, flip LB back to previous target group. For k8s deployments: kubectl rollout undo deployment/control-plane --namespace redwood.
- For container registries: keep previous image digest pinned in the release artifacts so a restart can use exact earlier image.
Data-affecting rollback (DB migrations):
- Only run irreversible migrations in maintenance windows with DB backups and verified restore steps.
- Prefer backward-compatible migrations: add new columns nullable, backfill in separate step, then switch reads to new column.
- If forced to rollback post-migration: restore DB from snapshot, re-run safe schema-aligned runtime (use older runtime image), rehydrate caches from persisted snapshots if available.

Safety checks and monitoring to enable during rollout:
- Enable request sampling and detailed tracing for first two waves (increase retention temporarily).
- Golden prompt set: run a fixed set of inference prompts through candidate and baseline and compare outputs for semantic drift; threshold failure if >X% divergence.
- Alerting: p50/p95 latency > baseline+50ms, error rate >0.5% increase, or token cost deviation >10% should auto-trigger rollback.

Terraform module migration notes (practical tips):
- When splitting a large module into smaller ones, create an intermediate compatibility layer: deploy the new modules in shadow with separate state first, then switch consumers.
- For provider version upgrades that change resource lifecycle, do it in a separate PR and schedule a canary apply to a non-critical env.
- Use module version tags in consumption layers instead of HEAD; pin in environment configs.

Test harness & smoke checklist (to run per wave):
- health/readiness endpoints respond within 200ms
- tokenization sanity for sample prompts produces same token counts (within margin)
- KV cache hit rate for warmed keys >= 70% on second wave after warmup
- SDK integration smoke: basic text generation, embeddings, and a function call test pass
- Observability: logs contain new structured fields and do not exceed retained quotas (watch log ingestion costs)

Customer communications and support playbook:
- Pre-upgrade: post in #private-deploy-upgrades, send customer email 72h prior with planned window and rollback SLA.
- During: update status page and Slack escalation channel every 15–30m for the first hour.
- Post-upgrade: share short summary of checks run, any observed regressions, and mitigation steps. Attach PR links and migration notes.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Define exact semantic-diff thresholds for "golden prompt" acceptance. (assign: Maya)
- Add automated terraform state mv dry-run script to CI (assign: Arjun)
- Formalize API deprecation header format and SDK linter checks (assign: Diego)

Appendix: quick commands and recovery snippets
- Rollback control-plane k8s: kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/control-plane --to-revision=<previous-rev>
- Pin previous image: kubectl set image deployment/control-plane control-plane=<registry>/control-plane@sha256:<digest>
- Restore DB (example): pg_restore -d redwood_prod_restored < snapshot-file> && run migrate-down.sh --target-version=<x>
- Terraform state mv example: terraform state mv "module.old.module[0].resource_name" "module.new.resource_name"

Notes: keep this doc light and action-oriented; translate to a checklist-runbook in the operations runbook system after we've validated steps in a staging run.
